what: Every passage Townsend (2025) discusses as tied, or not tied, to Adam Clarke's commentary, keyed from the article itself. Each 'changes' entry is [Isaiah verse as placed by lab.isaiah, King James words, Book of Mormon words] of a change Townsend names; it is looked up by exactly those words in the variant list. 'outside' says why a named change is not in our variant set. 'primary' is the index of the change Townsend ties to Clarke in that example (added 2026-11-24 after the first lookup output, see the judging card).
source: Colby Townsend, 'Early Nineteenth-Century Biblical Scholarship and the Production of The Book of Mormon', Journal of the Bible and its Reception 12:1 (2025) 57-84, doi 10.1515/jbr-2024-0001 (held privately: data/private/lab/sources/papers/townsend2025_biblical_scholarship.pdf). Jackson pages: Interpreter 66 (2025) 131-150.
clarke_edition_townsend: 1825 New York, Abraham Paul, vol. 3 (p. 65 n. 33); ours is the same printing: internet_archive:holybiblecontain0003adam

claim_strength.p64: argues Smith had access to Clarke and used it in an idiosyncratic, eclectic way; links said to be unique to Lowth, Clarke and the book among English commentaries before 1830
claim_strength.p66: 'convinced, based on the evidence', that Smith dictated Isaiah out of Clarke's volume

counts_given: none: no number of variants checked, no number matched, no comparison with other commentaries

items.jackson: 'then' added at four other Isaiah verses Clarke does not touch; verb-first after 'then' is usual

items.outside: a 40-word addition, longer than max_edit_words, so listed but not searched or judged; and the claim is about cross-references, not a reading
items.jackson: Nephi's own comment between Isaiah verses; the word links are loose
in Clarke the fish are dried up; in the book the waters are, and the fish still stink

items.clarke_reading: when he ariseth to strike the earth with terror (line added to v. 10)
items.kind: Clarke restores a line; the book adds a different one
items.jackson: no word in common; the KJV 'for' read as 'because' explains the added verb

items.clarke_reading: cedars as princes; hills as kingdoms, states (note on vv. 13-16)
changes: soon cometh upon all nations yea
and upon all the nations which
items.jackson: no shared wording; the conclusion is 'incomprehensible'

items.kind: Townsend says Clarke does not account for it; credits Wesley 1765, William Lowth 1739, Scott 1824, Parish 1813, Ethan Smith 1811
items.outside: an 8-word addition, longer than max_edit_words, so listed but not searched or judged
items.jackson: prints the passage; does not discuss 'ships of the sea'
Clarke reads 'its joy' (lo for lo'), not a bare deletion; 'not' widely held a scribal error

items.outside: the clause added at the start of 14:4 opens 1830 paragraph bom:465 before the first aligned words, so the aligner reads it as a preface, not a variant
items.jackson: 'in that day' is in KJV Isaiah 40+ times; nothing in Clarke suggests the added clause
'the nations' is far commoner in the KJV; all English Bibles before the KJV had the plural

items.clarke_reading: for how would my name be blasphemed; Syriac and Vulgate first person
items.jackson: one shared pronoun is not evidence

items.clarke_reading: hearken unto me, O ye distant lands
items.outside: the book's words come before the verse, which itself is unchanged; the aligner reads them as a preface
items.jackson: the verse is unchanged; Townsend compares the added preface

items.clarke_reading: I cannot read it; for it is sealed up
items.outside: 2 Nephi 27 rewrites Isaiah 29 too freely for the aligner to place its words on verses
items.jackson: 'read it' comes after a long insertion; 'sealed up' was the common idiom
